snippet.description:
Artists have described it for centuries: the muse visits, lightning strikes, the idea just arrives. Neuroscientist Heather Berlin says there’s a reason creativity can feel like it comes from outside you. In flow states, a part of your brain called the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex quiets down, and with it, your sense of self starts to dissolve. Meaning maybe the muse was you all along. Watch Unexplainable on Netflix or listen wherever you get your podcasts.
